newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - March 21.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

The Guardian newspaper has alleged that PM John Major was aware former minister Tim Smith had accepted 18,000 stg from Harrods boss Mohamed Al Fayed a month before he was forced to resign. The Labour Party is renewing pressure on the government to publish the full report by Sir Gordon Downey into parliamentary sleaze.

Lloyds Bank has been criticised for not following the Greenbury code on executive pay and allowing its directors to set each others salaries. Peter Brown of the Top Pay Research Group said the Lloyds renumeration committee should have the final on pay not the board.
BASS DEAL DECISION 'ON HOLD FOR ELECTION'

The Board of Trade is likely to drag its feet on a decision over brewing group Bass' acquisition of Carlsberg-Tetley until after the general election. A report by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission on the deal's impact on the brewing industry is likely to be passed to the DTI on Monday.
PITFALLS IN SHOPPING FOR GERMAN FIRMS

Chancellor Helmut Kohl is understood to have intervened in steel group Krupp's hostile bid for rivals Thyssen and ordered talks about a limited joint venture instead of a take-over. Robert Fleming analyst Robert Gibson said the deal could have opened a relatively closed German economy to bids from outside the country.
